sources.source: Modern slavery: NRM and DtN statistics, January to March 2026
sources.verified_fact: The official Q1 2026 release records 6,003 National Referral Mechanism referrals, including 656 referrals reporting exploitation in Greater London. A referral may name multiple exploitation locations, so county totals overlap and must not be combined.
sources.quality_effect: Adds modern-slavery safeguarding context with referral, hidden-population and overlapping-geography guards; referrals are not prevalence estimates or parcel-level risk.

sources.source: Supplementary information on referrals to the NRM made prior to an arranged return from the UK, 2025
sources.verified_fact: The 26 June 2026 official ad hoc release is operational management information specifically about NRM referrals made before arranged returns from the UK during 2025.
sources.quality_effect: Adds a narrow operational-cohort guard; the release cannot be treated as the full NRM population, a local exploitation rate or a parcel-safety measure.

sources.source: Police recorded knife-enabled robbery offences, year ending March 2026
sources.verified_fact: The first regular quarterly release reports 12,650 knife-enabled robbery offences in the year ending March 2026 across seven participating police forces, 21% below the June 2024 baseline. The figures are provisional and come from live force systems.
sources.quality_effect: Adds a current knife-enabled robbery trend check while enforcing seven-force coverage, baseline and provisional-live-system limits; it is not a complete national or parcel-level series.

sources.source: Police National Computer proxy for knife-enabled offenders
sources.verified_fact: The experimental measure identifies 9,106 proxy knife-enabled offenders in 2023 by matching a knife-possession offence with one of seven potentially knife-enabled offences occurring on the same date. It covers cautions or convictions and is not equivalent to police-recorded knife-enabled crime.
sources.quality_effect: Adds an offender-side cross-check with explicit experimental, same-date inference and justice-outcome selection guards; it must not be used as incident prevalence or local risk.

sources.source: Police powers and procedures: Roads policing, to December 2024
sources.verified_fact: The 19 March 2026 release covers 2024 roadside breath tests, positive or refused tests, fixed penalty notices, driver retraining, court action and cancelled notices, including force-level breath-test rates per 1,000 population.
sources.quality_effect: Adds roads-enforcement context while separating police activity and disposal outcomes from collision exposure, road danger and parcel-access safety.

sources.source: Police custody and pre-charge bail, year ending March 2025
sources.verified_fact: The official release covers police custody, strip searches, pre-charge bail, release under investigation and voluntary attendance. Several forces could not provide complete pre-charge bail data, and key bail analyses use data from 39 forces and are designated Official Statistics in Development.
sources.quality_effect: Adds custody-process context with incomplete-force, process-change and development-statistic guards; custody or bail records are not unique-person incidence or parcel risk.

sources.source: Seizures of drugs in England and Wales, financial year ending 2025
sources.verified_fact: The accredited release records 269,321 drug seizures in the year ending March 2025, 24% more than the previous year. It states that enforcement activity, recording practices and market changes affect the series, and notes that the Metropolitan Police introduced a broader recording system in February 2024.
sources.quality_effect: Adds drug-market enforcement context with activity, recording-change and authority-mix guards; seizure counts must not be interpreted as drug prevalence or parcel-level threat.
